autotest: initial content of string utils This CL adds string utils module with a function which joins strings with length limit. The direct reason we need this join function is to handle URL with many query parameters, e.g. in RPC of GS cache. If the HTTP request longer than a pre-defined value, HTTP servers may response with 414 error (URI too long). In order to resolve this problem, we must split the request to some sub-requests and each only handle part of query parameters, e.g. GET /extract/control_files.tar?file=control_file1&file=control_file2 GET /extract/control_files.tar?file=control_file3&file=control_file4 ... We can use the join function to generate these sub-requests, e.g. for q in join_longest_with_length_limit(['file1', ...], MAX_LEN, separator='&file='): url = '/extract/control_files.tar?file=' + q ... CHROMIUM: cros_ec: handle MKBP more events flag CL:1341159 adds a "more events" flag to allow the EC to notify us that there are more MKBP events waiting to be served. This CL extends the cros_ec bottom-half IRQ handler to listen to that flag in order to try and serve all known events before returning to the kernel with IRQ_HANDLED. This serves an optimization purpose as it minimizes the round-trip back and forth from the interrupt handler, and it also improves the quality of sensor timestamping, as it avoids a mismatch of event times between EC and AP that can confuse the median filter we use in the sensor ring. As described in the EC CL, this change is forward and backward compatible. BACKPORT: FROMGIT: arm64: dts: rockchip: Add 32k clk on rk3399-gru This adds the 32k clock to the RK3399 Gru board file, which is provided by a Silego oscillator on Gru boards. Even though it's not directly used, muxes will end up traversing the entire clk tree on calls to determine_rate if it doesn't exist. This is because the 32k clk is listed as a possible parent on some clks. Since the clk doesn't know about the 32k clk (it was never registered), it triggers a global search for it. This can happen about 40 times per second, which isn't great for power.
